hero.lede: A civic-tech platform mirroring Riigikogu open data. Every fact links back to its official source — no opinion, no ranking.

split.body: Riigiluup does not interpret, evaluate or produce rankings. Every vote, every bill and every metadata field contains a direct link to the official Riigikogu form — and the sync log shows when every row was last updated.
split.quote: «If you cannot verify the source, you cannot trust the system.»
split.step1P: Riigikogu OpenData API — roll-call votes, bills, members. Votes every 6 hours, the rest once a day.
split.step2P: Idempotent pipeline into PostgreSQL. Every record carries source_hash and fetched_at fields.
split.step3P: Presented as-is, without interpretation. Every row links back to the original form.
split.step4P: Every error can be reported. The correction is public, signed and versioned.

hero.lede: Ten visualizations built purely on open data. Every number is traceable to a Riigikogu form. No opinion, no ranking — only what the votes, attendance and bills themselves say.

agreement.note: Each cell shows how often two factions reached the same majority choice. The diagonal is self-comparison — always 100%. Data only from named votes where both parties had a clear majority.

discipline.note: Top-24 MPs who most often voted against their faction's clear majority choice. Named votes where the faction had an actual majority.

flow.note: What passes and what gets stuck — initiated, in committee, 1st/2nd/3rd reading, adopted or rejected. Every flow is traceable to the official proceeding page.

attendance.note: Each row = one MP, each column = one attendance check (last 40). Blue = present, red = absent. Right column shows attendance %.

timing.note: 7 weekdays × 24 hours. Dark blue = peak activity. Late-night voting is exceptional and worth asking about.

topics.note: By Eurovoc topics. Tile size = number of bills, blue darkness = share adopted.

velocity.note: Distribution of adopted bills from initiation to acceptance. Left = fast (potentially rushed), right = slow (potentially important and contested).

scatter.note: X-axis: how much the MP votes with the coalition (+1) vs opposition (−1). Y-axis: how loyal to their faction (+1) or dissident (−1). Values computed from actual votes, not declared position.

cospons.note: Every black edge that cuts through the centre is a bill that united MPs from different parties. Visibility across party lines that would otherwise go unnoticed in statistics.

night.note: Riigikogu's usual sitting hours are weekdays 08:00–20:00. Every named vote outside that window or on weekends is listed here — with time, margin, and linked bill. Doesn't automatically mean something's wrong, but it deserves scrutiny.

about.title: About Riigiluup
about.intro: Riigiluup is a public, open-source tool that makes the work of the Estonian Riigikogu easier to follow. It aggregates the parliament's own open data — MPs, roll-call votes, and bills — and presents it as neutral profiles, timelines, comparisons, and analytics. It covers the current Riigikogu (2023–2027), with roll-call voting records reaching back to 2019, and every figure links back to the official Riigikogu source.
about.editorialBody: The service does not assign ideological labels, moral scores, or rankings — it is a mirror, not an interpreter. It reports factual counts and rates and lets you draw your own conclusions. Where a metric could be misread, we document the formula, what is included, what is excluded, and the known limitations; a figure is never framed as good or bad, only described and linked back so you can check it against the original Riigikogu form.

list.members: Member profiles, faction, committees, electoral district.
list.bills: Bills (eelnõu), their stages, sponsors, and Eurovoc topic tags.

index.title: Methodology
index.intro: Each metric on this site follows an explicit formula. The pages below describe how numbers are computed, what is counted, what is excluded, and what the numbers do NOT tell you.

agreement.title: Pairwise agreement methodology
agreement.intro: Pairwise agreement measures how often two MPs cast the same comparable choice on votes where both actually voted.
agreement.same: Same: both MPs cast the same comparable choice (both FOR, both AGAINST, or both ABSTAINED).
agreement.different: Different: both cast comparable choices but they differ.
agreement.separateHeading: What is reported separately, NOT in the rate
agreement.separate: At least one MP did not participate (did-not-vote, absent, attendance-check presence).
agreement.interpretation: A high agreement rate says the two MPs, when both voting, made the same choice most of the time. It does not measure ideological similarity in general; it only measures overlap on this specific set of votes in this specific time window.

alignment.title: Group alignment methodology
alignment.intro: Group alignment measures how often an MP's vote matches their parliamentary group's majority position. It is a factual comparison, not a judgment about loyalty or independence.
alignment.eligible1: The MP cast a comparable choice (FOR, AGAINST, or ABSTAINED).
alignment.eligible2: The MP's group cast at least one comparable choice.
alignment.eligible3: The group had a clear majority — a single choice strictly outnumbered the others. A tie is NOT a clear majority.
alignment.matchBody: Among eligible votes, the MP's choice equals the group's majority choice.
alignment.excludedHeading: What is intentionally excluded from the rate
alignment.excluded1: Did-not-vote and absent — displayed separately as "recent deviations" and via voting-participation.
alignment.excluded2: Votes where the group split evenly (no clear majority).
alignment.interpretation: A high group alignment says the MP voted the same way as most of their group when a majority position existed. It does not say the MP agrees with every group position, and it does not say the group's position is correct or incorrect. A low alignment simply means the MP diverged on some votes with a clear group majority; the deviations list shows which.

participation.title: Participation methodology
participation.votingFormula: rate = (FOR + AGAINST + ABSTAINED) / every roll-call vote in which the MP held a mandate
participation.participatedBody: Participated counts every roll-call vote where the MP cast FOR, AGAINST, or ABSTAINED.
participation.excludedN1: Did-not-vote (present but did not press a button).
participation.excludedN3: Neutral (a rare procedural status used by the Riigikogu API).
participation.excludedBoth: Excluded from BOTH numerator and denominator:
participation.excludedB2: Secret votes (no per-MP records are published).
participation.excludedB3: Votes where the MP did not have an active mandate.
participation.votingSourceLine: Computed from the roll-call votes ingested from Riigikogu — the same ones listed under Votes. The primary source of each vote is the endpoint
participation.sittingFormula: rate = sittings attended / total sittings in the period
participation.sittingBody: This is the official participation figure Riigikogu publishes from its own data (the "sittings" field). We mirror it as reported, without recomputing. It reflects whether the MP was registered as attending the sitting, and is not a full-time presence measure.
participation.attendanceBody1a: Attendance checks are a specific procedure in the Riigikogu where members register presence at a sitting.
participation.attendanceBody1b: This is NOT total working hours or a full-day attendance measure.
participation.attendanceBody2: A high attendance-check rate does not mean an MP is present for the entire sitting or every committee. A low rate does not mean the MP was absent from all work — they may have been in committee meetings, official trips, or on leave.
participation.attendanceWhyDiff: This is usually lower than sitting attendance: an MP can attend the sitting yet miss a specific, momentary quorum check (stepped out, working in committee). It is a stricter, per-moment measure.
participation.attendanceSourceLine: Computed from our ingested quorum-check records. The primary source of each check is the endpoint
participation.periodBody: Metrics on MP profiles default to the current parliamentary term — the 15th Riigikogu, starting 2023-04-10. When Riigikogu reports "0 of 0", the rate is displayed as an em dash ("—") rather than 0%.

analytics.title: Analytics methodology
analytics.intro: Every chart on /analytics is a single SQL aggregate over the ingested Riigikogu data — no imputation, no interpolation, no ML. This page lists each computation's exact formula, its filter set, and what it does NOT tell you. Source of each query:

velocity.heading: Bill velocity histogram
velocity.body: Only bills with phase = ADOPTED and both dates non-null are counted. Buckets: ≤ 1 week, ≤ 1 month, ≤ 3 months, ≤ 6 months, ≤ 1 year, > 1 year.
velocity.note: Does NOT measure "how fast" any single reading was — only end-to-end initiation to adoption. Bills withdrawn, rejected, or still pending are excluded.

flow.heading: Bill flow (Sankey)
flow.body: Links between phases are simple counts: initiated → {committee | first-reading | submitted | other}, first→second→third-reading, third-reading → adopted, first-reading → {rejected | withdrawn}, committee → in-readings. Reading counts are per-item (a bill that had four separate first-reading events is still 1).
flow.note: This is a snapshot of phase counts, NOT a longitudinal flow. Some links are approximations because Riigikogu does not tag every "outcome" directly to a reading in the API.

factionAgreement.heading: Faction agreement matrix
factionAgreement.body: A "clear majority" means a strict plurality of one comparable choice (FOR, AGAINST, or ABSTAINED) inside the faction on that vote. Ties do not count as a majority; attendance-checks are excluded.
factionAgreement.note: A high pairwise rate says the two factions' majorities coincided on the votes where both had one. It does NOT mean they agree ideologically — many coincidences are on procedural or unopposed motions.

cohesion.heading: Faction cohesion (party-of-week highlight)
cohesion.body: Restricted to votes from the last 30 days where the faction had a clear majority and the individual MP cast a comparable choice. Factions with fewer than 30 such votes in the window are excluded to keep the ranking stable.

discipline.heading: Discipline breakers (defection rate)
discipline.body: "Eligible" = the MP cast a comparable choice AND their faction had a clear majority on that vote. MPs with fewer than minEligible eligible votes (default 20) are excluded to avoid ranking based on 1–2 samples.

attendance.heading: Attendance matrix
attendance.body1: present_count = attendance checks where the MP's individual_vote choice was PRESENT, FOR, AGAINST, or ABSTAINED. recorded_count = attendance checks where the MP had ANY row at all — cells with no row are shown as "—" and don't count in either the numerator or denominator.
attendance.body2: MPs with recorded_count < ⌈N/5⌉ (i.e. seated for less than 20 % of the window) are filtered out so that partial-mandate MPs (substitutes, maternity/paternity leave, ministers) don't appear as false 20–40 %-tenders.

timing.heading: Vote timing heatmap
timing.body: Buckets: 7 rows Monday..Sunday × 24 columns 0..23. Timestamps are converted to Europe/Tallinn before extraction, so DST shifts are handled by Postgres.

night.heading: Night votes
night.body: Window is configurable per request (defaults 08:00–20:00 Europe/Tallinn). Only type = OPEN vote events are counted; attendance-checks are excluded.

topics.heading: Topic treemap
topics.body: Topics are Eurovoc descriptors emitted by Riigikogu on the bill detail endpoint. A single bill may map to several topics — it counts in each. Top-N by bill count is returned; the tail is not merged into "Other".

scatter.heading: MP similarity scatter
scatter.body1: Both axes are normalised to [-1, +1]. x → +1 means the MP tends to agree with the coalition majority over the opposition majority; x → −1 the opposite. y → +1 means the MP nearly always votes with their own faction's majority; y → −1 means they nearly always deviate.
scatter.body2: A small deterministic jitter (~4 %, seeded from the MP's slug) is added so that identical scores don't stack on top of each other visually. The underlying number used elsewhere on the site is unjittered.
scatter.note: This is a 2-D projection, not an ideological placement. Two MPs at the same coordinate voted similarly on the aggregate set — they may still disagree on any single issue.

cosponsorship.heading: Co-sponsorship graph
cosponsorship.body: Nodes: MPs with ≥ 1 sponsorship. Edges filtered by minWeight (default 2 shared bills) to keep the graph legible. Only sponsor_kind = PLENARY_MEMBER is considered — commission, government, and faction sponsorships are ignored for the graph.

streaks.heading: Attendance streaks
streaks.body: Uses the same "present" definition as the attendance matrix. MPs with fewer than N records (i.e. not seated the whole window) are excluded from the streak list rather than counted as broken.

tight.heading: Tight votes (smallest margin)
tight.body: Ranked ascending among type = OPEN vote events where both counts are > 0. Attendance checks and unanimous votes are excluded (they always yield a margin of 0 or a trivial one).

exclusions.heading: Common exclusions across all analytics
exclusions.item1: Attendance-check events are excluded from anything labelled "vote", because they are procedural presence-records and do not decide legislation.
exclusions.item2: Secret ballots publish no per-MP records, so they contribute nothing to per-MP rates.
exclusions.item3: Ties in faction-majority calculations are treated as "no clear majority" — those votes drop out of alignment/agreement rates.
exclusions.item4: MPs on partial mandates (substitutes, ministers, leave) are filtered from panels where a per-MP denominator would otherwise be misleading (attendance matrix, discipline breakers).

period.heading: Time period
period.body: All analytics on /analytics default to the entire ingested data window unless the panel exposes an explicit range picker. Attendance matrix uses the last N attendance checks (default 40) regardless of calendar date.

repro.heading: Reproducibility
repro.body: Every number on /analytics is the output of a single deterministic SQL query. The queries are in backend/src/main/java/com/politico/analytics/AnalyticsService.java (public repository) and can be reproduced against a local dump. If two runs of the same panel return different numbers with unchanged data, that is a bug — please report it via

sources.title: Data sources
sources.intro: All political data on Riigiluup is imported from official Riigikogu open data. Nothing is scraped, editorialized, or purchased.
sources.ep6: — MP photos, proxied through Riigiluup for caching.
sources.licenseBody1: Riigikogu open data is released under
sources.licenseBody1c: . This site's own aggregated content and code are released under the same license so downstream reuse is straightforward.
sources.updateBody: Votes sync every 6 hours (03:05, 09:05, 15:05, 21:05 Europe/Tallinn), so new roll-calls appear the same day. Members, factions, profile details and bills refresh once a day (04:30 Europe/Tallinn): they change slowly, and past records are immutable and never re-fetched. The "Last sync" badge in the header shows the timestamp of the last successful refresh.

dataStatus.title: Data freshness
dataStatus.intro: Riigiluup refreshes upstream Riigikogu data every 6 hours (03:05, 09:05, 15:05, 21:05 Europe/Tallinn). The table below lists the most recent successful runs of each ingestion job.
dataStatus.lim1: Riigikogu itself sometimes publishes vote or bill records with a delay of a few hours.
dataStatus.lim2: Riigikogu's statistics endpoints require a date window; the site queries them lazily and caches results per MP × date range.
dataStatus.lim3: Secret votes have no per-MP records upstream and appear only as aggregate counts.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.aboutVisitors: Nothing linked to your identity. There is no login, no cookies for tracking, no analytics platform, no advertising.
privacy.logs: The Nginx reverse proxy writes standard HTTP access logs (IP address, request URL, user-agent, timestamp) for operational reasons. Logs are retained for up to 30 days and then rotated out.
privacy.aboutMps: Only what is already a matter of public record via the Riigikogu: name, party, faction, electoral district, committee memberships, votes, speeches count, and the biography maintained by the MP or the Riigikogu chancellery.
privacy.np1: Home address, personal phone, private email.
privacy.np4: Social-media posts (only counts of official press mentions where reported by Riigikogu).
privacy.rightBody2: . Every record links to its official source; corrections at the source flow into Riigiluup on the next daily refresh.
privacy.photosBody: MP photos are cached from the Riigikogu file endpoint to reduce load on their servers. They are the property of the Riigikogu and are used under the CC BY-SA 3.0 license.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.licenseBody1a: The aggregated data displayed on Riigiluup is released under
terms.licenseBody1c: , the same license used by the underlying Riigikogu open data. You may reuse it — including for commercial purposes — provided you (a) credit Riigiluup and Riigikogu as sources, and (b) release derived data under the same license.
terms.licenseBody2: The site's source code is available under an OSI-approved permissive open-source license.
terms.warrantyBody: Riigiluup is provided "as is". Every fact is sourced from a public API and can change without notice. The site aims for accuracy but cannot guarantee it. Use the "Source ↗" link on any card, chart, or metric to verify against the original before making decisions.
terms.neutralityBody: Riigiluup does not endorse parties, factions, or individual members. It does not display "best" or "worst" rankings, ideological scores, or sentiment analysis. Where a computed rate could be misread, the methodology pages describe the formula and its limits.
terms.fairUseBody: Automated bulk scraping of Riigiluup's public REST endpoints is allowed within reason (≤ 1 req/s per IP, same as the upstream Riigikogu limit). For heavy programmatic use, prefer the upstream Riigikogu API directly.

corrections.title: Corrections
corrections.intro: Riigiluup mirrors Riigikogu's open data — most factual errors originate upstream and flow into Riigiluup on the next daily refresh once fixed at the source. If you spot an issue that Riigiluup introduces (a broken chart, a wrong slug, a mislabeled metric), please tell us directly.
corrections.step1: The URL or ID of the record you are reporting.
corrections.step2: What is currently shown and what should be shown instead.
corrections.buttonExplainerC: button below opens your mail client with that template pre-filled.
corrections.whatWeDo: Every credible report is reviewed by a maintainer within 7 days. If the issue is with Riigiluup's own presentation, it is patched and released. If the issue is with the upstream Riigikogu data, we forward it to Riigikogu's data team and note the report on this page.
corrections.wnd1: Retract public voting records — a vote is a public fact.
corrections.wnd2: Re-label MPs or parties on request.
corrections.wnd3: Assign or remove "activity scores" — the site does not compute them.
